runtimeEvidence.summary: Frost and Elemental community-import responses were blocked by active Community-release variant integrity before Resolver timing; direct read-only diagnosis found zero strict variant-key matches for normalized historical aliases.

The normalized alias repair reached the selected variant read, but Frost import remained blocked because the scoped option query required option rows to share the selected variant ID; the established Resolver authority query binds those sealed option keys to the Release instead.

Frost import reached a verified Resolver snapshot in 1.279 seconds but was correctly partial: the projector recognized enchants and embellishments yet rejected eight gem identities because active Release optionType is socket rather than gem.

Frost observed_profile_mage_frost cold import HTTP 200 verified in 862.969ms (release_read 820.847ms), 15 gear slots, 8 gems, 6 enchants and 2 embellishments; immediate warm import HTTP 200 verified in 74.476ms with cache hit.

Elemental observed_profile_shaman_elemental HTTP 200 verified with 16 gear slots, 6 gems, 5 enchants and 2 embellishments. Frost finger1 mode=slot response HTTP 200 retained gearPayloadMode=slot, gearSlot=finger1 and exactly one candidate group; stale Manifest returned HTTP 409 manifest_mismatch.
All 40 expected class/spec pairs returned HTTP 200 mode=initial and dataStatus=verified; all exposed templates were raiderio_observed_profile and every pair had one observed template.

Runtime SHA parity was 10/10; wow-backend, wow-gear-stat-snapshot-worker and nginx were active; ten WOW timers were active/waiting; failed units and candidate-window error-priority backend logs were empty. /health was OK while /api/data/health honestly remained overallStatus=partial.

A source-display loop had overwritten the sealed winner row, yielding HTTP 200 verified with data.template.id empty and causing the client identity fence to reject import. After the local red regression and variable-shadowing repair, Frost cold and warm import both returned template.id=observed_profile_mage_frost; the latter was a cache hit.
